conceptZh: 辣：辛加束，辣到想吐舌頭的味道。
object: a caped action-figure hero whose cape is too long, and a row of glossy red toy chili peppers
morph: the hero's flapping cape bumps one chili and sets off a domino pile-up that luckily lands as 辣
creativeAngle: 披風英雄的長披風碰倒第一根辣椒，連鎖骨牌倒成辣字，最後被辣到噴煙。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 辣 (spicy), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a caped action-figure hero whose cape is too long, and a row of glossy red toy chili peppers. Cool pale-mint backdrop so the red pops; the glyph is fire-engine red with a glossy shine. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: the caped action figure (teal cape trailing three body-lengths) swoops in on a bounce and lands in a hero pose; the voice says the first 辣 as the cape swishes across and nudges a standing chili. 1.5-3.0s: the chili tips into the next one and a long domino chain of toy chilies clatters across the frame while the hero trips over his own cape. The voice says the second 辣 as the pieces tumble and curl into the left radical. 3.0-4.5s: the last chili spins and lands as the final stroke, snapping the glyph into 辣; the hero pops his head out from under the cape and gasps. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 辣椒 (ㄌㄚˋ ㄐㄧㄠ) as a shiny chili hops up next to him, he takes a tiny sniff, and two small puffs of cartoon steam shoot out of his ears. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is still; the hero fans his face with the cape corner at the side. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Narration (off-screen, warm and unhurried, Taiwanese Mandarin, Ministry of Education readings, no erhua): the exact spoken line is 辣、辣、辣椒, syllable by syllable ㄌㄚˋ、ㄌㄚˋ、ㄌㄚˋ ㄐㄧㄠ. Two isolated utterances of the character, a short pause between them, then the word once, then silence; the voice must not add any explanation, translation or repeat. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 辣 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 短手橡膠恐龍搆不到高架上的大辣椒，只好坐上玩具機器人的湯匙投石器，結果馬力太強，牠飛過辣椒、撞翻一箱紅色積木條、彈牆後倒栽進水桶，散落的積木條一根根落定拼成「辣」字。
object: a squeaky green rubber dinosaur with huge flat feet and tiny useless arms, a boxy mismatched toy robot running a wooden spoon catapult, and a glossy red toy chili pepper on a tall pole
morph: the launched dinosaur crashes through a crate of red stick-shaped toy bricks; the scattered bricks rain down and each lands in place as one stroke of 辣 — 辛 on the left, 束 on the right — then everything freezes into a solid glossy red glyph
creativeAngle: 舊版是披風英雄推骨牌、辣椒冒火貼紙，比較安靜。這次改成很清楚的「發射」笑點：短手恐龍搆不到辣椒是目標，機器人馬力太強讓牠飛過頭是失誤，撞翻積木箱是大碰撞，散落的積木條拼成「辣」，最後辣椒正好掉進恐龍嘴裡，配上「辣椒」這個詞，噴出的蒸氣就是「辣」的意思，聽到的跟看到的是同一個故事。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright toy-animation clip, simple staging on a pale cream-yellow tabletop set with a soft light-blue wall, nothing busy behind. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 辣 (spicy), correctly formed (辛 on the left, 束 on the right), ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with clear margins, in saturated glossy chili red.

Cast: a squeaky green rubber dinosaur with enormous flat feet and comically tiny arms, eager and stubborn; a boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts, one arm longer than the other, whose motors always run too strong. Prop: a glossy red toy chili pepper on a tall pole at frame right.

0.0–1.5s: The dinosaur stares up at the chili, licks its lips, hops, and waves its tiny arms. They don't come close to reaching. It flops onto its belly with a squeak.
1.5–2.8s: The robot rolls in with a wooden spoon catapult and the dinosaur climbs into the spoon. The voice says the first 辣 as the dinosaur strikes a drumroll pose, tapping its belly with its tiny arms and squeezing its eyes shut. The robot's long arm yanks the lever and its motor whirs way too hard.
2.8–4.0s: WHOOSH. The dinosaur flies in a huge arc right past the chili, smashes through a small crate of red stick-shaped toy bricks, BOINGs off the far wall with rubbery squash-and-stretch and drops upside-down into a blue bucket at bottom left, feet kicking.
4.0–5.0s: The scattered red bricks rain down and clack into place one by one in the center, building 辛 and then 束. The voice says the second 辣 as the last strokes snap in, and the bricks fuse into one smooth glossy glyph 辣.
5.0–8.0s: Final hold. The glyph stays perfectly still and fully readable. At about 5.5s the voice says 辣椒 as the chili wobbles off its pole and drops straight into the upside-down dinosaur's open mouth. Its cheeks glow red, two small puffs of cartoon steam pop from its nostrils, and it kicks its feet happily. The robot gives a lopsided thumbs-up. All of this stays well clear of the strokes.

Narration: off-screen, warm and friendly, clear Taiwanese Mandarin with Ministry of Education readings and no erhua. The voice reads exactly 辣、辣、辣椒 (ㄌㄚˋ、ㄌㄚˋ、ㄌㄚˋ ㄐㄧㄠ) slowly and distinctly with clear tones and a short pause between utterances, then stops. No other speech, and no music louder than the voice.

Only the glyph 辣 appears as text: no subtitles, captions, labels, logos or watermark. No flashing effects, no dark grading, and only stylized toys, no people. The bonks are harmless.
